properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 29 at 9:24AM CDT until October 2 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
The weather pattern on Wednesday will begin to change as an
approaching upper level low over the southwestern U.S. weakens the
subtropical ridge axis over Texas and the western Gulf. Isolated to
scattered showers and thunderstorms will develop during the daytime
hours. A Pacific cold front will move into the region Thursday
spreading showers and thunderstorms over more of the area. Rainfall
totals from Wednesday evening through Friday will be 2-4 inches with
isolated amounts up to 8 inches possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Texas, including the following
counties, Atascosa, Bandera, Bastrop, Bexar, Blanco, Burnet,
Caldwell, Comal, Dimmit, Edwards, Frio, Gillespie, Gonzales,
Guadalupe, Hays, Kendall, Kerr, Kinney, Llano, Maverick, Medina,
Real, Travis, Uvalde, Val Verde, Williamson, Wilson and Zavala.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is a potential for life threatening flooding
somewhere in the watch area. Excessive runoff may result in
flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their
banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.
Low-water crossings may be flooded. Extensive street flooding and
flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rainfall totals of 2-4 inches with isolated amounts of 8 inches
are possible.
- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
San Antonio, Austin, Round Rock, New Braunfels, Cedar Park,
Georgetown, San Marcos, Pflugerville, Medina, Schertz, Kyle, Del

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Pecos River Above Pecos affecting San Miguel County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pecos River above Pecos.

* WHEN...From this morning to late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 5.0 feet, Fast flowing water may erode banks and
approach homes near the river.  Private bridges could drive
localized flooding as debris accumulates along the upstream sides.
Further rises may make bridges unsafe to cross and isolate
residents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:00 AM MDT Tuesday the stage was 3.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this morning to a crest of 5.1 feet this afternoon. It will then
fall below flood stage this evening.
- Flood stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 5.1
feet on 05/21/1991.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 900 PM MDT.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 28 at 2:42PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Light rain and snow will meander around the Interior. Locations
above 2000ft have the highest chance for snow through Monday
night but snow levels continue to drop to 1000ft Tuesday. Valley
locations, including Fairbanks, may see some snowflakes mix in
with rain beginning Tuesday night with flurries lingering into
Wednesday. Little to no accumulation is expected in the valleys
through Wednesday afternoon. Between 1000-2000ft, up to 1 inch of
snow is possible but there will be melting as the snow reaches the
ground. Above 2000ft, 1 to 3 inches of snow is possible through
Wednesday afternoon. Another round of light snow is becoming more
likely Wednesday night into Thursday with minor accumulations
possible, even in Fairbanks.

travel conditions in Isabel Pass beginning Monday night. Cooler
temperatures are expected to settle in through midweek which
could allow for 3" to 6" of snow through Wednesday morning.

morning. This could be the start of the permanent snow pack.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 25 at 2:21PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

In the wake of today's precipitation, our attention will turn to the
Eastern Pacific. Tropical moisture is anticipated to spread across
the Desert Southwest early next week, drawing moisture from a pair of
Hurricanes; Odalys and Polo. The forecast becomes increasing complex
due to a closed low currently forecast to drive across the Southwest
CONUS as Hurricane Polo approaches the Baja California Peninsula.
Strong southerly winds ahead of the low are expected to pull tropical
moisture towards eastern Utah and western Colorado as early as Monday
morning. The challenge and uncertainty in our precipitation forecast
increase as the week progresses and the low traverses our southern
States. Excessive rainfall is most probable over AZ and NM, attm, but
the northerly extent poses a threat to our southern San Juan river
basins. Current forecasts suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain over Monday
morning through Wednesday. At face value, rivers and tributaries will
see a bump up due to said moisture. However, localized heavier
amounts could result in minor flooding across the southern San Juan
foothills and communities further downstream.

Rivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated
soils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of
additional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar
response. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in
several creeks and rivers than what has been observed over the
previous 7 days. However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts
(i.e. above 90th percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action
stage to minor flooding. Most probable basins to see significant
rises include; the Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito
Creek, and the Animas River Basins.

Convective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said
tropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across
the CWA, however, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San
Juans. Please continue to monitor the forecast as these systems
evolve. Especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in
the southwest quadrant of the forecast area.
